sentences.show: Every morning, a six-year-old girl walked to school past a crowd. One woman held up a black doll in a coffin.
On this day in 1960, she became the first Black child at an all-white school in New Orleans.
Seeing the crowd, she later said, she thought it was Mardi Gras.
White parents pulled their children out. All the teachers but one refused to teach her.
Barbara Henry, from Boston, taught her alone, for over a year.
A woman threatened to poison her, so the marshals let her eat only food from home.
Her family paid too. Her father lost his job, and the grocery store turned them away.
But neighbours walked behind the marshals' car to school.
Fifty years later, President Obama told her: "If it hadn't been for you guys, I might not be here."
Also on this day: Apollo Twelve launched, and a plane first took off from a ship.
